notes: Posted 26 May 2026, version 2 (2 June 2026) submitted to PRL; listed on the DES home page. The 3.0σ CMB-combination figure appears in the abstract sentence beginning "Finally, when combined with primary CMB information".

significance.quote: The combination yields $w_0=-0.84^{+0.10}_{-0.10}$ and $w_a=-0.44^{+0.60}_{-0.55}$, the tightest constraints ever obtained from a single survey, with $2.2\sigma$ deviation from a cosmological constant.
significance.value: 2.2σ deviation from a cosmological constant (full DES: SNe Ia, BAO and 3×2pt); 2.3σ with DESI DR2 BAO added; 3.0σ with primary CMB added

summary.plain: Using supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations and weak lensing with galaxy clustering from the full six-year Dark Energy Survey, the collaboration tested whether dark energy changes with time. It finds a 2.2σ deviation from a cosmological constant, rising to 3.0σ when CMB data are added.
summary.technical: Full-DES SNe Ia + BAO + 3×2pt in the w0wa model: w0 = -0.84 ± 0.10, wa = -0.44 (+0.60, -0.55), 2.2σ from a cosmological constant; adding DESI DR2 BAO: 2.3σ; adding primary CMB: w0 = -0.82 ± 0.05, wa = -0.63 (+0.21, -0.18), 3.0σ.

title: Constraints on Dynamical Dark Energy from Multiple Probes in the Full Dark Energy Survey
why_it_matters: The abstract says the full-DES combination gives the tightest dark-energy-evolution constraints from a single survey and that the best-fit parameters across probe combinations are consistently in the region w0 > -1 and wa < 0.
